title: Machine learning-derived intracellular protein-based prognostic model reflecting a senescence-associated secretory phenotype-driven immunosuppressive microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma.
authors: Chang X, Jiang L, Zhang L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the associations of senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related genes with the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and clinical outcomes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and to develop and evaluate a prognostic signature for risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction.
METHODS: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was conducted to identify distinct molecular subtypes. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), Random Forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were utilized to identify core prognostic SASP genes. The expression patterns of selected SASP-related genes were explored using multi-omics datasets, LUAD cell lines, and clinical specimens.
RESULTS: Cluster 1 was associated with significantly shorter overall survival (OS), enhanced senescence pathway activity, and computationally inferred immunosuppressive and immune-exclusion features. Five intracellular SASP regulators-ANGPTL4, CDKN2A, H2AX, MMP1, and CCL20-were selected through machine learning to construct the SASP Protein Regulator Score (SASP-PRS). A high SASP-PRS was associated with the activation of senescence/SASP and cell-cycle pathways, suppression of antitumor immune signatures, and distinct immune-checkpoint and chemokine expression profiles. A higher SASP-PRS was also associated with advanced disease stage, poorer OS, predicted lower responsiveness to immunotherapy, lower predicted sensitivity to erlotinib, and higher predicted sensitivity to selected chemotherapeutic agents. The nomogram incorporating the SASP-PRS demonstrated discriminatory ability and calibration for predicting 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS in the analyzed LUAD cohorts.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that SASP-related gene-expression patterns are associated with LUAD molecular subtypes, senescence signaling, computationally inferred immune features, and treatment-related outcomes. The SASP-PRS may serve as a potential biomarker for prognostic stratification in LUAD. However, its utility for treatment-response assessment remains exploratory. Prospective external validation and functional studies are required to establish its clinical applicability and clarify the mechanisms linking SASP-related networks to the LUAD immune microenvironment.

title: Live-cell FRET imaging-based efficacy prediction of EGFR-TKIs in EGFR L858R-mutant NSCLC.
authors: Li X, Dai L, Yang P et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Functional assays can assist individualised selection of treatment regimens by evaluating the ex vivo response of tumour cells to anticancer therapeutics. However, the two major strategies used to assess responses to targeted drugs, target-based profiling and phenotypic profiling, have inherent limitations. Target-based profiling does not directly capture downstream cell-fate outcomes, whereas phenotypic profiling provides limited mechanistic information on drug action.
METHODS: Live-cell fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) microscopy was used to integrate the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 with cellular phenotypic features, thereby predicting the efficacy of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) at the single-cell level.
RESULTS: The target-based drug score (T-score), derived from the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 in living cells co-expressing CFP-EGFRL858R and YFP-GRB2, enabled evaluation of the on-target activity of EGFR-TKIs against EGFRL858R. The phenotype drug score (P-score), constructed from cellular phenotype features, characterised the phenotypic responses induced by EGFR-TKIs. The TP-score, integrating the T- and P-scores, accurately predicted the efficacy of EGFR-TKIs. In living H3255 cells, the TP-score of osimertinib (OSI) was higher than that of gefitinib (GEF). Notably, in H3255 cell-derived xenograft (CDX) mouse models, OSI showed superior in vivo antitumour efficacy compared with GEF. Furthermore, live-cell TP scoring revealed that primary tumour cells from a patient with NSCLC did not respond to OSI, a finding consistent with the absence of actionable EGFR mutations in this patient.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the clinical feasibility of predicting EGFR-TKI efficacy by integrating EGFRL858R-GRB2 interactions with cellular phenotypic features in single living cells.

title: Clinical and molecular prognostic factors associated with outcomes of first-line osimertinib in EGFR-Mutated advanced NSCLC: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Ruan Y, Xue H, Long C et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is the standard first-line therapy for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but outcomes remain heterogeneous. This meta-analysis evaluated baseline clinical and molecular prognostic factors associated with poorer outcomes in this setting.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 20 May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with EGFR-mutated advanced, recurrent, or metastatic NSCLC receiving first-line osimertinib with extractable prognostic data. The primary outcome was progression-free survival or real-world progression-free survival (PFS/rwPFS); overall survival or real-world overall survival (OS/rwOS) was secondary. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Eighteen studies involving 4,070 first-line osimertinib-treated patients were included. TP53 mutation was associated with shorter PFS/rwPFS (HR 1.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-2.37) and worse OS/rwOS (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.14-2.12). EGFR L858R, versus exon 19 deletion, was associated with shorter PFS/rwPFS (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39-1.90) and worse OS/rwOS (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.40-1.88), with consistent estimates across sensitivity analyses. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status ≥ 2, central nervous system/brain metastasis, and liver metastasis were associated with poorer outcomes. The OS/rwOS association for liver metastasis was sensitive to alternative estimate selection. Evidence for bone metastasis and programmed death-ligand 1 expression was less robust.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence-tier assessment identified EGFR L858R, ECOG PS ≥ 2, and CNS/brain metastasis as high-certainty adverse prognostic factors. Liver metastasis was supported by moderate certainty for PFS/rwPFS but lower certainty for OS/rwOS. TP53 mutation, PD-L1 expression, and bone metastasis were lower-certainty or exploratory findings. These findings support future integrated prognostic models, but do not establish criteria for selecting intensified first-line therapy over osimertinib monotherapy.

title: ERO1A promotes lung cancer progression via HIF1A/EGFR.
authors: Liu Y, Lin Y, Zhou Y et al.
abstract: Globally, lung cancer has emerged as a formidable public health challenge and is the primary cause of cancer-related deaths. The role of ERO1A in lung adenocarcinoma has been rarely explored. Here, we identified significant overexpression of ERO1A in lung cancer tissues, which correlates with reduced patient survival rates. Silencing ERO1A notably suppressed cell proliferation, clonogenic formation, migration, and invasion in lung cancer cell lines. ERO1A inhibition impairs tumor growth in murine models. RNA sequencing and proteomics analyses following ERO1A knockdown revealed that ERO1A is involved in multiple oncogenic pathways, particularly EGFR and HIF1A. ERO1A modulates HIF1A/EGFR may through H₂O₂. The oncogenes MET, CCND1, and p21 may also be involved in the ERO1A regulation pathway. The upregulation of ERO1A may serve as a valuable diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in lung cancer. The ERO1A-HIF1A/EGFR axis may represent a potential therapeutic target.

title: Clinicopathological and molecular features of lung carcinomas with abnormal SMARCA2 expression and preserved SMARCA4/SMARCB1.
authors: Wei H, Liang J, Li H et al.
abstract: The clinicopathological significance and molecular basis of abnormal SMARCA2 expression in lung carcinoma remain poorly understood. We retrospectively analyzed 16 poorly differentiated lung carcinomas showing complete loss or diffuse marked reduction of SMARCA2 expression with preserved SMARCA4 and SMARCB1. The tumors exhibited a broad morphological spectrum and were classified as adenocarcinoma (n = 10), non-small cell carcinoma favoring adenocarcinoma (n = 2), squamous cell carcinoma (n = 3), or non-small cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified (n = 1). Clinical molecular testing revealed diverse molecular alterations, including KRAS, EGFR, ALK, TP53, PIK3CA, and CD274 abnormalities. Targeted SMARCA2 sequencing, performed in 11 cases, identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic alterations in four tumors without recurrent hotspot mutations. DNA methylation analysis of two CpG-rich regions, performed in nine cases, did not identify a consistent hypermethylation pattern within the analyzed regions. These findings demonstrate considerable morphological and molecular heterogeneity among lung carcinomas with abnormal SMARCA2 expression and preserved SMARCA4/SMARCB1. Recurrent SMARCA2 hotspot mutations and consistent hypermethylation of the analyzed CpG-rich regions were not identified, indicating that additional mechanisms may contribute to abnormal SMARCA2 expression.

title: Rapid Regression of Choroidal Metastasis under First-Line Osimertinib Therapy in Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Case Report.
authors: Hufnagel HJ, Zeitz O, Abdula F et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Choroidal metastases may cause substantial visual impairment in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although local ocular treatments are frequently considered, targeted systemic therapy may provide effective control in tumors harboring actionable mutations. We report the rapid regression of a choroidal metastasis following first-line osimertinib therapy in a patient with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated NSCLC.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man with metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC presented with progressive visual decline in the left eye. Ophthalmic examination revealed a peripapillary choroidal lesion associated with serous retinal detachment. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated subretinal fluid, consistent with a choroidal metastasis. First-line osimertinib therapy had been initiated 12 days before presentation at our clinic. An early reduction in subretinal fluid was observed during follow-up, followed by complete resolution at the 2-month follow-up. This was accompanied by regression of the choroidal lesion and improvement in visual function. No local ocular treatment was required.
CONCLUSION: First-line osimertinib may induce rapid regression of choroidal metastases in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. In selected cases, an early response to systemic targeted therapy may allow local ocular treatment to be avoided.

title: Risk Factors for Renal Injury in Lung Cancer Patients Receiving Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Inhibitor Therapy.
authors: Qin L, Zheng C, Chen Z et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Renal injury is an adverse effect of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) inhibitor therapy. We investigated factors associated with renal injury and renal outcomes by VEGF inhibitor type in lung cancer.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 441 lung cancer patients treated with VEGF inhibitors. The primary cohort comprised 376 patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2, negative dipstick proteinuria, and no hematuria at baseline; 65 patients underwent exploratory analysis. The primary composite renal outcome was incident proteinuria and/or eGFR decline >20% from baseline within 1 year. Cox models adjusted for clinical, tumor, and treatment covariates. Landmark and overlap-weighted sensitivity analyses were performed. Proteinuria and eGFR decline were analyzed separately.
RESULTS: The primary composite renal outcome occurred in 250 patients (66.5%); among patients with an event, the median time to first event was 92.0 days. Diabetes mellitus (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.17-3.05), higher body mass index (BMI) (aHR per 1-kg/m2 increase, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.09), and lower hemoglobin (aHR per 10-g/L increase, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.79-0.94) were independently associated with the primary outcome. VEGF inhibitor type was not associated with the primary outcome (overall p = 0.690), with similar overlap-weighted results. Incident proteinuria occurred in 120 patients (31.9%) and was associated with diabetes and lower hemoglobin; eGFR decline >20% occurred in 188 patients (50.0%) and was associated with lower hemoglobin. Platinum-containing chemotherapy showed a time-varying association with incident proteinuria.
CONCLUSION: The primary composite renal outcome was common during the first year of VEGF inhibitor therapy. In the primary cohort, diabetes mellitus, higher BMI, and lower baseline hemoglobin were associated with this outcome, whereas no statistically significant association was observed for VEGF inhibitor type. These findings warrant validation in independent cohorts.

title: Case Report: Coexpression of somatic EGFR, BRCA1, and BRCA2 mutations in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Negin A, Sachdeva K, Weiss J
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved dramatically over the past decade with the advent of widespread genetic testing, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies. Treatments directed against epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and other driver mutations have reduced toxicity and improved efficacy for selected patients.
CASE PRESENTATION: We present a 59-year-old man with metastatic NSCLC harboring coexisting EGFR, BRCA1, and RNA-binding motif protein 10 (RBM10) mutations and high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. A BRCA2 mutation was later detected on peripheral blood testing. The patient presented with a debilitating stroke that included dysphagia and hemiparesis. During his course of care, he received osimertinib, after which EGFR and RBM10 variant allele frequencies (VAFs) increased on peripheral blood testing. He also received immunotherapy and olaparib. Despite high response rates reported in the literature, he did not respond to these agents. He had a response to chemotherapy but tolerated it poorly. Ultimately, given the lack of durable response and his inability to tolerate chemotherapy, the patient opted for palliative care.
DISCUSSION: Patients with actionable targets such as EGFR, BRCA1/2, or elevated PD-L1 generally have superior outcomes with targeted and combination therapy compared with patients who lack targetable options. However, coexisting mutations can interact and provide escape mechanisms. The lack of response in our patient is consistent with studies showing reduced efficacy of EGFR-directed therapy in the presence of RBM10 loss-of-function (LOF) alterations. Further research in patients with multiple concurrent mutations is needed to improve treatment options for this group.

title: Rat sarcoma inhibitors in and beyond gynecologic malignancies.
authors: Dwabe S, Samaeekia R, Cristea M
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent advances in direct rat sarcoma (RAS) inhibition and downstream pathway targeting have created novel therapeutic strategies which can be utilized in gynecologic oncology. This review examines RAS biology, lessons learned from other malignancies, and emerging strategies for gynecological malignancies.
RECENT FINDINGS: KRAS G12C inhibitors in lung cancer established the clinical feasibility of direct RAS targeting, while colorectal cancer studies demonstrated the importance of lineage-specific combinations. KRAS G12D inhibitors, targeted protein degraders, and multiselective RAS(ON) inhibitors represent the next frontier in RAS inhibition, expanding therapeutic options across both gynecologic and nongynecologic tumors. In recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, therapeutic advances have centered on inhibiting the downstream RAS-mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)-extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling pathway using MEK or combined RAF/MEK and focal adhesion kinase inhibitors, rather than direct RAS inhibition, demonstrating encouraging clinical responses, leading to accelerated approval for KRAS-mutant disease.
SUMMARY: RAS-pathway directed therapy requires consideration of tumor lineage, specific alleles, and functional pathway dependence. Although clinical progress in gynecologic oncology is most relevant in low-grade serous ovarian cancer, emerging non-G12C therapies warrant further evaluation across gynecologic malignancies. Novel combinations and integrated biomarkers will be necessary to improve patient selection and overcome therapeutic resistance.

title: Peripheral immune tolerance as a driver of tumor immune escape and therapy resistance.
authors: Vaishnave S, Jayaraj A, Selvaraj J et al.
abstract: Peripheral immune tolerance, essential for preventing autoimmunity, is increasingly co-opted by tumors to drive progression, metastatic dissemination, and immunotherapy resistance. Whereas central tolerance eliminates autoreactive clones, peripheral tolerance remains dynamically regulated by antigen persistence, cytokine gradients, metabolic cues, and stromal architecture, a plasticity that tumors exploit to build a multilayered immunosuppressive ecosystem. This narrative review synthesizes multi-omic, spatial, cellular, and molecular evidence, emphasizing 2021 to 2025 publications alongside foundational studies, to propose tumor-induced peripheral tolerance (TIPT) as a unifying framework for immune escape and treatment failure. TIPT emerges from coordinated suppression by tumor-resident regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory B cells, M2-like macrophages, tolerogenic dendritic cells, and exhausted CD8? T cells, sustained by suppressive cytokine networks, metabolic deprivation, epigenetic fixation of dysfunctional states, and stromal-vascular exclusion barriers. Spatially organized tolerance niches are associated with immune evasion, metastatic seeding, and resistance to checkpoint blockade. Strategies targeting suppressive cell populations, metabolic pathways, chromatin regulators, and stromal barriers are in clinical development, but clinical benefit has been established for only a limited subset, and anti-TIGIT antibodies failed to meet primary endpoints in phase 3 lung cancer trials. Machine-learning models show promise for predicting tolerance states and guiding combination design, but prospective clinical validation is still needed. TIPT may represent an important, potentially actionable determinant of tumor evolution and immunotherapy response, and durable cancer control is likely to require combined strategies that dismantle this tolerance ecosystem.

title: Dual Checkpoint Inhibition With or Without Chemotherapy in Metastatic NSCLC: A Reconstructed Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis.
authors: Taylor S, Mamede I, Gazzoni G et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dual immune checkpoint inhibition (DICI) is an established first-line treatment for metastatic NSCLC. Whether the addition of chemotherapy provides an incremental survival benefit beyond DICI alone remains unclear.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis of trials evaluating first-line DICI and DICI plus chemotherapy (DICI-CT) in metastatic NSCLC. Data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards and time-varying models. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to PD-L1 expression, histology, and STK11 or KEAP1 mutational status.
RESULTS: Four trials comprising 1654 patients were included (699 receiving DICI-CT and 955 receiving DICI). Median OS was similar between the groups (15.4 versus 15.0 mo, hazard ratio = 0.93, 95% confidence interval: 0.81-1.08). Proportional hazards assumptions were violated, and time-varying analyses suggested modest late survival differences favoring DICI, with higher 5-year OS (19.4% versus 17.1%) and progression-free survival (10.5% versus 8.2%). In STK11-mutated tumors, DICI-CT was associated with a limited early survival benefit that was not sustained over time. No clear differences were observed in KEAP1-mutated tumors.
CONCLUSIONS: The addition of chemotherapy to DICI was not associated with improved survival in an unselected population of patients with metastatic NSCLC. These findings support an individualized approach to the use of chemotherapy in combination with DICI.

title: Baseline prevalence of lung cancer screening and associated factors among women in breast cancer screening clinics prior to the Pink & Pearl program: A retrospective analysis of electronic health records.
authors: Odeny B, Ramaswamy SG, Bowe B et al.
abstract: Lung cancer screening (LCS) remains underutilized, with 18% uptake nationally, despite established evidence-based guidelines, particularly among women who engage with preventive care through breast cancer screening (BCS). We characterized baseline LCS uptake and its correlates among women receiving BCS at two participating hospitals. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using six years of electronic health record data (October 2019-November 2025) from Barnes-Jewish West County Hospital and Christian Hospital. Women aged 50-80 with any documented smoking history were included. The primary outcome was LCS uptake, defined as evidence of at least one low-dose computed tomography scan. We conducted multivariable logistic regression models and assessed for effect modification by race and area deprivation using likelihood ratio tests. Results Of 9,686 women with smoking history, 3,209 (33.1%) had received at least one LCS. Pack-year documentation status (AOR 2.90; 95% CI: 2.63, 3.19), tobacco cessation medication use (AOR 2.21; 95% CI: 1.98, 2.48), and current smoking (AOR 1.84; 95% CI: 1.64, 2.07) were the factors most strongly associated with uptake. Non-Hispanic Black women had lower adjusted odds of obtaining LCS compared to non-Hispanic White women (AOR 0.87; 95% CI: 0.78, 0.98); estimates in the smaller pack-year subgroups were similar in direction but imprecise. Alcohol use was associated with lower odds of LCS uptake (0.81, 95% CI: 0.73, 0.89). Effect modification by race and area deprivation were not significant. Conclusions Baseline LCS uptake exceeded the national average; however, racial disparities were observed. Completeness of smoking history documentation, tobacco cessation medication use, and current smoking status were strongly associated with LCS uptake. These findings highlight the need for strategies to improve smoking history documentation and promote tobacco cessation efforts in cancer screening programs and establish the baseline against which the Pink & Pearl program, a co-located breast and lung cancer screening initiative at these sites, will be evaluated.

title: Improving equity in respiratory disease outcomes in Africa using data-driven tools: National Institute of Health Care and Research's (NIHR) EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project.
authors: Rudan I, Ozoh OO, Agbre-Yace ML et al.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pneumonia, influenza, asthma, tuberculosis, lung cancer, and COVID-19 are all prevalent in Africa, where they cause a very large burden on the population's health, but are managed by health systems with a limited capacity for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. They are also underlaid by substantial inequities in outcomes, with the poorest who have no access to care being affected the most. An interdisciplinary group of academics, policymakers, representatives of non-governmental organisations (NGOs), patients, and civil society are implementing a programme to address key respiratory diseases (RD) in five African countries where morbidity and mortality from RD is very large: Nigeria, Kenya, Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire, and South Africa. The aim is to build capacity, conduct quality research and an intervention trial, and engage communities and policymakers in order to achieve demonstrable and equitable reductions in morbidity and mortality from RD through evidence-based improvements in prevention, diagnosis, treatment, interventions, and policies. The EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project will map the landscape of respiratory medicine in partner countries through rapid reviews of the available literature and data; engage relevant in-country stakeholders; study patients' and providers' preferences and needs; identify research priorities using the Child Health and Nutrition Research Initiative method; and conduct summer schools for capacity building in data science and machine learning/artificial intelligence, in community engagement, and in advocacy for and the use of the Equitable Impact Sensitive Tool (EQUIST) and Pathways to Survival (PATHS) tool. The project will also assess national health system preparedness for emerging infections, identify bottlenecks for early response, assess oxygen capacity and security, study adherence to international guidelines, and conduct qualitative studies to understand barriers to seeking care. It will also explore the feasibility of delivering a pulmonary rehabilitation programme through a randomised controlled trial. Ultimately, the programme will link evidence with policy using the EQUIST and PATHS tools to improve equity in outcomes and identify bottlenecks that lead to morbidity and mortality from respiratory causes. Through high-level meetings, it will prioritise the implementation of equitable interventions that are appropriate to each African context and tailored to patients' needs. A team of social scientists and NGOs, joined by a team of researchers of diverse backgrounds, will engage communities, stakeholders and policymakers to build capacity through summer schools, and disseminate the results through a dedicated project website, the Journal of Global Health, the Journal of the Pan-African Thoracic Society, collaborating NGOs, and mainstream and social media.

title: Garsorasib (D-1553) in Combination With Pembrolizumab and Chemotherapy for First-Line Metastatic NSCLC With KRAS G12C Mutation: Results of a Phase 1b Study.
authors: Yan D, Liu C, Li X et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Garsorasib (D-1553) is an orally administered selective KRAS G12C inhibitor. We report results from group 1 of the phase 1b D1553-101 study assessing garsorasib plus pembrolizumab and platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC.
METHODS: Eligible participants had locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with KRAS G12C mutation and were candidates for pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy. Participants received garsorasib 600 mg once daily or twice daily combined with pembrolizumab 200 mg once every 3 weeks plus 4 to 6 cycles of cisplatin or carboplatin and pemetrexed (nonsquamous histology) or carboplatin and paclitaxel (squamous histology). The primary end points were safety and the incidence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs).
RESULTS: As of February 24, 2024, 17 participants received garsorasib 600 mg once daily (n = 10) or twice daily (n = 7) combined with pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy. Overall, 94% of participants experienced grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs), and 88% had a dose reduction or interruption due to treatment-related AEs. One participant in the twice-daily group experienced a DLT of grade 2 diarrhea; no other DLTs occurred. Among all participants, the objective response rate was 59%, and the median progression-free survival was 7.4 months.
CONCLUSION: In participants with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, despite an encouraging signal of efficacy, the incidence of treatment-related AEs with garsorasib plus pembrolizumab and platinum-based chemotherapy was high, and participants frequently had dose modifications or interruptions due to treatment-related AEs. Based on these findings, the study did not proceed to phase 2.

title: Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery versus Thoracotomy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Survival Analysis and Exploratory Predictive Modelling.
authors: Makarov V, Baimukhametov E, Yessentayeva S et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study retrospectively compared outcomes of minimally invasive and open surgical approaches for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a cohort of 255 patients operated on between 2014 and 2018. A machine-learning analysis was performed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating component.
METHOD: Survival was analysed by disease stage using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Because the groups were not randomised and were imbalanced at baseline, comparisons are unadjusted and should be interpreted as associations. Exploratory predictive models were developed using five machine-learning algorithms (random forest performing best), with feature contributions interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Missing values were handled by multiple imputation, continuous variables were standardised, and correlated features were excluded.
RESULTS: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was used more frequently for adenocarcinoma, in women, and at stage I, with zero postoperative mortality (0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy). At stage I, there were no differences in median overall survival (65.3 versus 67.7 months; p=0.768); at stage II, VATS was associated with longer survival (75.8 versus 48.8 months; p=0.003); at stage III, a similar direction did not reach significance. Recurrent predictors in the exploratory models were coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, intervention volume, tumour histology, and vascular invasion; however, test accuracy remained low (0.39-0.48), precluding clinical use. SHAP analysis highlighted resection completeness, lack of conversion, and tumour morphology.
CONCLUSIONS: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.

title: Closed Versus Open Vent Port Techniques and the Disconnection Technique for Optimizing Lung Collapse With Bronchial Blockers in Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Yao J, Chen YJ, Shen FM et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: For patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for lung cancer or other pulmonary lesions, effective one-lung ventilation (OLV) is essential to provide surgical exposure. Bronchial blockers (BBs) are increasingly used for OLV, but the optimal management of their vent port to accelerate lung collapse remains unclear.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, controlled trial, 75 patients were allocated to three groups (n = 25 each): Group 1-BB with vent port closed; Group 2 (control)-BB with vent port open; Group 3-BB with the disconnection technique. Primary outcome was the time to complete lung collapse, which was scored according to the video clips obtained during the operation. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hypoxemia, blood gas analysis, blocker malposition, perioperative complications, and surgeon satisfaction.
RESULTS: A total of 72 patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, with 24 patients in each group. Median time to complete lung collapse was 15 min (95% CI: 10-15) in Groups 1 and 3 but was not reached in Group 2 (15/24, 62.5% had not achieved complete collapse by 30 min). In an exploratory 30-min restricted mean survival time (RMST), complete collapse occurred on average 14.17 min earlier in Group 1 (95% CI: 11.10-17.23) and 12.50 min earlier in Group 3 (95% CI: 9.62-15.38) than in Group 2, with no difference between Groups 1 and 3 (1.67 min, 95% CI: -1.85 to 5.19); time-averaged hazard ratios were consistent (Group 1 vs. 2, 9.80 [4.22-22.73]; Group 3 vs. 2, 7.63 [3.36-17.31]; Group 1 vs. 3, 1.20 [0.67-2.16]). No significant differences were detected in hypoxemia, blocker malposition, or complications across groups; however, the trial was not powered for safety outcomes.
CONCLUSION: In patients aged 18-65 years with ASA I-II and normal pulmonary function undergoing thoracic surgery, the closure of the BB vent port results in a more rapid lung collapse compared to maintaining the vent port open. However, there was no statistically significant difference observed between the vent port closure technique and the disconnection technique regarding the time required for complete lung collapse.
